what_it_does: Lichen optimizes processors that have different instruction set architectures (ISAs) on the same chip—for example, some cores that are efficient for simple tasks and others designed for complex workloads. Current systems switch between core types at coarse program phases (large sections of code), missing finer optimization opportunities. Lichen dynamically morphs between different instruction sets and execution modes (in-order execution for simplicity versus out-of-order execution for performance) at a granular level. A machine learning model (CART decision tree) predicts which configuration is optimal for each fine-grained phase, automatically adapting the hardware for the current workload.
